architectūra, architectūrae f.

noun, first declension

architecture, the art of building

The subject of Vitruvius’s ten books; Cicero names it, with medicine, among the arts that call for real knowledge and are honourable for those whose station they suit.

Examples

  • quibus autem artibus aut prūdentia major inest aut nōn mediocris ūtilitās quaeritur, ut medicīna, ut architectūra, ut doctrīna rērum honestārum, hae sunt iīs, quōrum ōrdinī conveniunt, honestae

    but the arts that call for more wisdom or bring no small benefit, such as medicine, architecture and the teaching of honourable things, are honourable for those whose station they suitCic. Off. 1.151 (Lewis & Short, s.v. ars)

See also architect, build, profession.
